samples.summary: No test asserts the copy/cut keydown is NOT preventDefault-ed — the exact property the #870 fix depends on
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2298-2299 returns `true` for mod+c/x deliberately *without* calling `e.preventDefault()`, because in a real browser preventDefault on the keydown suppresses the native `copy`/`cut` event and nothing would ever be written (the original #870 symptom). Every test in copy-integrity.test.ts synthesizes the clipboard event by hand (`dispatchClipboard` at line 87, called after `pressCopyShortcut`), so the keydown and the clipboard event are fully decoupled: adding `e.preventDefault()` in the image key handler would keep all 20 tests green while Cmd/Ctrl+C over a selected image silently writes nothing again. `pressCopyShortcut` creates a `cancelable: true` event (line 124-126) but no test ever reads `event.defaultPrevented` on it — contrast the copy-event tests at lines 437/460, which do assert `defaultPrevented`.

samples.summary: Cut inside a table cell (the other consumer of the rewritten getSelectedBlocks) is never tested
samples.evidence: `sliceBlockRange`/`blockParentMap` resolution (text-editor.ts:3739-3775) is reached from both `handleCopy` and `handleCut` (line 1247). All four #872 tests (lines 213-292) use `dispatchCopy` only; no test cuts a rich selection out of a table cell. Cut is the higher-stakes path — a payload regression there deletes the content and puts nothing on the clipboard (data loss), whereas the copy case merely loses formatting.

samples.summary: The 'both endpoints share one cell' assumption behind the cell branch is asserted only in a comment, never in a test
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:3742-3746 comments that `normalizeRange` guarantees both endpoints are in the same cell, then uses only `start.blockId` to pick the block list; if `end` were elsewhere `sliceBlockRange` returns [] (empty clipboard). No test in copy-integrity.test.ts selects across a cell boundary or from a cell into body text — the multi-block test (line 246) keeps both blocks inside the same cell.

samples.summary: Copying a click-selected image in a read-only document is untested, although read-only copy is exactly what the context-menu change enables
samples.evidence: The read-only cases in this file cover only refusal to delete (line 480) and refusal to cut (line 578). `handleCopy` has no read-only guard, and docs-context-menu.tsx now shows Copy in read-only, so read-only copy is a newly-reachable user path; the only existing read-only copy test (editor-read-only.test.ts:229) asserts `text/plain` alone and never inspects the WAFFLEDOCS_MIME payload or an image selection.

samples.summary: The modifier gating of the new copy/cut branch is only exercised in its all-modifiers-set form; Shift/Alt exclusion and the per-platform modifier branch are untested
samples.evidence: `pressCopyShortcut` always sets BOTH `metaKey` and `ctrlKey` (line 125), so the `navigator.platform` branch at editor.ts:2295-2297 can never distinguish a wrong choice — a handler that read the wrong modifier would still pass. Nothing tests `!e.shiftKey && !e.altKey` (editor.ts:2298): e.g. Cmd+Shift+C should fall through to the catch-all and clear the image selection, and no test pins that.

samples.summary: Ordinary multi-block body-text rich copy through the refactored sliceBlockRange has no direct coverage
samples.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks` was rewritten to route the non-table case through `sliceBlockRange(layout.blocks.map(lb => lb.block), ...)`. The only new test hitting that path is the single-block 'image selection is ignored when there is also a text selection' case (line 364); a grep of packages/docs/test shows only list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts and image-paste-merge.test.ts reference WAFFLEDOCS_MIME, and editor-read-only.test.ts:229 asserts text/plain only. A regression in multi-block body slicing (styles or boundary trimming) would silently lose formatting on the most common copy of all.

samples.summary: 'a read-only editor cuts nothing' passes on a pre-existing guard, not on the new image cut code
samples.evidence: `handleCut` returns at text-editor.ts:1219 for read-only before the new `imageSelectionProvider` branch is reached, so `written.size === 0` holds regardless of whether the new image-cut logic is correct. Real behavior, but it is not coverage of the code this diff added.

samples.summary: Test (e) asserts only that a mocked editor.copy() was called
samples.evidence: `makeEditor` stubs `copy: vi.fn()`, so `expect(copy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` proves wiring only; the claim in the diff comment that copy actually works in a read-only editor is carried by docs' editor-read-only.test.ts:229, which checks text/plain alone. Acceptable at the component boundary, noted for completeness.

finding.summary: No test asserts the copy/cut keydown is NOT preventDefault-ed — the exact property the #870 fix depends on
finding.evidence: editor.ts:2298-2299 returns `true` for mod+c/x deliberately *without* calling `e.preventDefault()`, because in a real browser preventDefault on the keydown suppresses the native `copy`/`cut` event and nothing would ever be written (the original #870 symptom). Every test in copy-integrity.test.ts synthesizes the clipboard event by hand (`dispatchClipboard` at line 87, called after `pressCopyShortcut`), so the keydown and the clipboard event are fully decoupled: adding `e.preventDefault()` in the image key handler would keep all 20 tests green while Cmd/Ctrl+C over a selected image silently writes nothing again. `pressCopyShortcut` creates a `cancelable: true` event (line 124-126) but no test ever reads `event.defaultPrevented` on it — contrast the copy-event tests at lines 437/460, which do assert `defaultPrevented`.

verdict.reason: The claimed gap is real. editor.ts:2281-2300 consumes mod+c/x by returning true WITHOUT preventDefault (explicit comment at 2289-2294), and text-editor.ts:854-856 just returns, so nothing else cancels the keydown — the "consumed but not cancelled" property is exactly what makes the native copy/cut event still fire and is the crux of the #870 fix. No test observes it: pressCopyShortcut (copy-integrity.test.ts:123-127) builds a cancelable keydown but returns void, so the event object is unreachable and defaultPrevented can never be read on it; the clipboard event is then synthesized independently by dispatchClipboard (line 96), fully decoupling the two, so inserting e.preventDefault() at editor.ts:2299 would keep all tests in the file green. The only defaultPrevented assertions in the file (437, 460) are on the hand-built copy event, not the keydown. Searching wide for a counterexample found none: repo-wide grep for defaultPrevented yields no docs-package keydown assertion (only copy-integrity 437/460 and editor-contextmenu 94/103 on contextmenu events); selectImageAt/getSelectedImage appear in no other test file; other metaKey users in packages/docs/test (pending-style-editor, visual-line-affinity, editor-read-only, backward-selection-toggle, editor-on-cursor-move) never press mod+c/x with an image selected; and there is no e2e suite or colocated src test covering it. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: the untested property, if broken, silently returns Cmd/Ctrl+C over a selected image to writing nothing (the original user-visible #870 symptom) with full green coverage.
